text.arabic_uthmani: وَمَا نَقَمُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction fused to the following negation; it links the witness scene to an explanatory denial rather than adding a detached event

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negative particle opening the grievance denial

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) carries the prior witness scene (85:7) into an explanation of motive. It is not bare addition: the conjunction resumes the narrative and makes the following negated grievance clause answer why the violence happened. Because it is written and heard with {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}), the turn into explanation and the denial arrive together, so the verse opens its motive statement already as a cancellation of the alleged charge.

topics.headline: resumptive motive link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the conjunction turns the prior witnessed violence (85:7) into an exposed motive statement, not just another event.
topics.reason: The aligned particle begins the verbal clause and attachment evidence licenses the whole following unit as the negated grievance clause.

topics.headline: connector and negator arrive together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the explanatory turn and the negation as one onset before the hard grievance verb lands.
topics.reason: The surface sequence binds {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) directly to {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}), matching the row's fusion and cadence claim.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening the restrictive frame; it voids the grievance before the exception names faith as the only stated cause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negated grievance verb
exceptive particle completing restriction

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) negates {{ar:نَقَمُوا۟}} ({{tr:naqamū}}) before any cause is named, so the clause first empties the accusation. With the later {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}), it forms restriction: every charge is excluded except the believers' faith. The particle therefore does more than report no grievance; it denies the moral validity of the blame-register and makes the final exception self-indicting.

topics.headline: accusation voided first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause cancels any valid charge before the faith-clause appears.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence show {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) negating the perfect verb, so the CRITICAL claim about frontloaded cancellation survives.

topics.headline: negation plus exception isolates faith
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) works with {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) to make faith the only stated basis of resentment.
topics.reason: The translation-support evidence explicitly marks the {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) ... {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) restriction and warns that faith must remain the sole stated cause.

topics.headline: fused onset and long-vowel frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the negating boundary as part of the verse's form, from fused {{ar:وَمَا}} ({{tr:wa-mā}}) to the later long-vowel exception.
topics.reason: The local order supports the sound-row claim without changing the grammar.

words.gloss_range: they resented, found fault, or moved toward punitive blame; local syntax leaves no direct object and exposes faith as the only recoverable cause
words.root_gloss_range: fault-finding, resentment, punitive displeasure, and vengeance branches; the local Form I perfect plural selects hostile grievance without making believers grammatically cause the blame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional target or source phrase
believers' faith verb in the exception clause

words.prose: {{ar:نَقَمُوا۟}} ({{tr:naqamū}}) is a completed plural act of hostile grievance, but it names no direct object. The verb must reach outward to {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) for the targeted group and to the exception clause for the alleged cause, which leaves no independent offense standing. Its {{ar:ن ق م}} ({{tr:n-q-m}}) field brings fault-finding, resentment, and punitive displeasure into one marked register; local Form I keeps culpable agency with the resenters, while related revenge and causative forms only sharpen the background. Parallels with resentment against belief or divine favor (5:59; 9:74) reinforce the inversion: the charge exposes the accusers. The shared plural cadence with {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}) makes the opposition audible, one group resenting and the other believing.

topics.headline: no direct offense is named
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hostile verb cannot name a standalone crime; target and cause have to be supplied outside it.
topics.reason: The verb instance confirms no direct object and a frame completed by {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) plus the clausal exception.

topics.headline: plural perfect records group action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that resentment is presented as an accomplished collective act, not a vague attitude.
topics.reason: The perfect third masculine plural morphology and discourse subject evidence support the collective completed-action reading.

topics.headline: blame range with revenge pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a marked prosecution-like resentment register, while the local Form I stops short of replacing the surface verb with explicit revenge or causation.
topics.reason: Reference evidence licenses the broader {{ar:ن ق م}} ({{tr:n-q-m}}) field, but the local surface is Form I, so derivative revenge and causative branches are retained only as pressure.

topics.headline: resentment against belief repeats
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 85:8 joining a wider pattern in which resentment against belief or divine favor turns into self-indictment (5:59; 9:74).
topics.reason: The supplied rows give concrete references, especially 5:59 and 9:74, and the local object of resentment is belief in God.

topics.headline: hostility and faith share plural cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a formal pairing between the persecutors' collective resentment and the believers' collective faith.
topics.reason: The two plural verbs stand in the same clause and share final plural cadence while their semantic fields oppose blame and trust.

words.gloss_range: prepositional pronoun phrase marking the believers as source, target, or relation of the grievance, not a simple direct object

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: faith verb whose subject resumes the same believer group

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) keeps the grievance relational. The preposition lets the clause say that fault was sought from, in relation to, or against them, while avoiding a direct-object accusation. The suffix carries the believers from 85:7 into the motive clause, then the same group reappears as the subject of {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}). That routing makes the victims the targeted group and the agents only of faith, not of any named offense; it also contrasts grievance sought from them with faith attached to God.

topics.headline: grievance is sought from them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase leaves the accusation relationally open: nothing direct is charged, yet the believers are where grievance is sought.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) the governed prepositional complement of {{ar:نَقَمُوا۟}} ({{tr:naqamū}}), matching the source-target CRITICAL rows.

topics.headline: same group crosses roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the believers move from target of grievance to subject of faith without changing groups.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence resolves the suffix to the preceding believers and also resolves the subject of {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}) to the same group.

topics.headline: grievance-source versus trust-object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between grievance sought from the believers and faith attached to God.
topics.reason: The local prepositional phrases attach to different heads and separate the targeted believers from the divine object of trust.

words.gloss_range: exceptive particle completing the restriction; it pivots from negated grievance to the sole surviving faith-clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negative particle paired with the exception
full verbal faith clause admitted by the exception

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) is the hinge where negation becomes restriction. It does not add a side detail; it closes the field opened by {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) and admits only {{ar:أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:an yuʾminū}}) as the remaining content. Because the exception is a full verbal clause, the persecutors' case reduces to an enacted relation of faith, and the lengthened recitation at the hinge lets the move from no charge to the only alleged charge be heard.

topics.headline: only faith survives the negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception does not defend a charge; it exposes that faith is the only charge left.
topics.reason: The attachment and translation-support evidence mark a restrictive {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) ... {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) frame with faith as the sole stated cause.

topics.headline: a full faith-act fills the slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception is not a noun label but a verbal act of believing.
topics.reason: The following {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) clause is licensed as the excepted content after {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}).

topics.headline: the exception hinge is audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the restriction as a boundary, with the long sound of {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) balancing the earlier {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}).
topics.reason: The local particle order supports the cadence and boundary rows without adding a new grammatical claim.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive particle that nominalizes the following belief verb as the excepted content and cause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: dependent belief verb governed by the particle

words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) packages the following verb as the thing singled out by the exception. It governs {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}), visible in the dependent mood, so the faith-clause is not an independent aside but the content of the accusation. Its content-and-cause value lets the clause mean both that they believe and because they believe. After the lengthened exception particle, the glottal entry of {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) makes the only charge begin with an audible catch. The accepted variant with explicit pronoun and perfect faith-form keeps the same causal slot but presents the faith as completed fact rather than ongoing dependent action.

topics.headline: belief-act becomes the charge-content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a full act of believing is treated as the sole item in the restrictive slot.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the subordinate faith clause that attachment evidence identifies as the excepted content.

topics.headline: the verb is dependent on the particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the belief verb is grammatically subordinated to the exception rather than narrating a separate event.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence says {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) governs {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}).

topics.headline: variant shows act and identity profiles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant evidence can frame the same accused faith either as ongoing action or established identity, while the local canonical parse remains subjunctive.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as contrast, but the canonical local surface remains {{ar:أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:an yuʾminū}}).

topics.headline: hamza marks the charge entry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a catch at the start of the only charge after the lengthened exception particle.
topics.reason: The sound row is local to the transition from {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) to {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}).

words.gloss_range: they believe, trust, or enter a faith relation; locally a Form IV dependent plural verb completed by the bā-governed divine name
words.root_gloss_range: faith, trust, security, safety, entrusting, and refuge branches; the local Form IV with {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) selects believing in or trusting God, while safety and entrusted-fidelity imagery remains active as pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: subordinating particle governing the faith verb
prepositional complement naming the object of faith

words.prose: {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}) is the act left standing after the restriction: the believers are accused of believing. Its missing final indicative marker keeps it dependent on {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}), and its complement comes immediately through {{ar:بِٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:bi-llāhi}}), so the charge concerns trust attached to God, not private opinion. The {{ar:أ م ن}} ({{tr:ʾ-m-n}}) field keeps security, trust, and entrusted-fidelity resonance (33:72) in view; Form IV selects committed faith, while safety-seeking or safe-conduct branches remain only background pressure. The root also crosses the local boundary from the believers named in 85:7 to the accused act in 85:8 and later believer language (85:10; 85:11), making identity and action converge. Its plural long-ū cadence answers the earlier plural resentment verb before the sound settles into the divine name.

topics.headline: faith is relational attachment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the alleged offense is not generic belief but trust attached to the named divine object.
topics.reason: The verb instance and attachment evidence show a Form IV faith verb completed by the {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) complement.

topics.headline: faith remains inside the exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is dependent content under {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}), not a freestanding report.
topics.reason: The final nūn omission and attachment evidence support subjunctive dependency.

topics.headline: victims act only as believers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the role contrast: persecutors perform resentment, while the targeted group performs only faith.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence resolves the subject of {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}) to the same believers marked by {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}).

topics.headline: security pressure inside faith
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief carries trust and security imagery under threat, while the local Form IV does not turn the clause into a request for safe-conduct.
topics.reason: The root field supports safety and entrusting pressure, but QAC fixes the local form as Form IV faith with {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}), not Form X seeking protection.

topics.headline: faith as act and fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical verb keeps believing active and ongoing, while variant evidence shows the same charge can also be framed as established belief.
topics.reason: The canonical surface is the dependent imperfect verb, while the cited variant is retained as contrast rather than as the governing parse.

topics.headline: faith root binds identity and outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the faith root linking the victims named in 85:7, the accused act in 85:8, entrusted-fidelity resonance (33:72), and later believer references (85:10; 85:11).
topics.reason: The rows provide same-surah references and the 33:72 entrusted-field comparison; these support a thread without overriding local grammar.

topics.headline: sound pairs resentment and faith
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the plural faith verb answer the plural resentment verb before the cadence settles into the divine name.
topics.reason: The two plural verbs are both local and semantically opposed, so the cadence observation is anchored.

words.gloss_range: prefixed preposition marking the object and attachment point of faith; locally bound to the divine name

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divine name governed by the faith preposition

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) completes the faith verb by attaching it to {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}). The preposition makes the sole charge specific: not belief in abstraction, but trust placed in God. Its proclitic form in {{ar:بِٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:bi-llāhi}}) makes that attachment visible and audible. The familiar faith-in-God formula is placed inside accusation here, and the same divine name then moves forward as witnessing subject in 85:9.

topics.headline: preposition fixes where trust attaches
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offense is specified by where faith is placed: in God.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) the {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}})-governed complement of {{ar:يُؤْمِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:yuʾminū}}).

topics.headline: attachment is visible and audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle is not visually or audibly loose; it binds directly to the divine name.
topics.reason: The local surface is the proclitic preposition attached to the divine name.

topics.headline: trust object becomes witness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a familiar faith-in-God formula placed inside accusation, then carried forward when the same name becomes witness in 85:9.
topics.reason: The formulaic row is locally constrained by the restriction frame, and the forward reference to 85:9 is explicit in the source row.

words.gloss_range: the proper divine name as the governed object of faith, then the head of the closing attribute phrase
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, refuge, devotion, and ultimate-authority pressure; the proper name locally functions as the fixed object of faith rather than a generic divine label

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is the endpoint of the {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}})-governed faith relation. The charge is therefore allegiance to the named God, not vague piety or social nonconformity. That familiar belief-in-God relation becomes the sole grievance here, echoing resentment-against-faith patterns (5:59; 9:74). The name also begins the closing attribute phrase: {{ar:ٱلْعَزِيزِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿazīzi}}) and {{ar:ٱلْحَمِيدِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamīdi}}) interpret the referent already fixed by the proper name. Root and derivation pressure keep worship, refuge, and overwhelmed devotion in view, while local grammar keeps the proper name as the selected faith-object. The same name then shifts from object of belief in 85:8 to witnessing subject in 85:9, tightening the answer to the persecutors' grievance.

topics.headline: the divine name anchors faith
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine name is grammatically bound to the faith verb as its object of trust.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence place {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) in genitive case under {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}), governed by the faith verb.

topics.headline: worship authority and refuge pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proper name carries worship-authority and refuge pressure, while the local function remains the fixed divine name after {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}).
topics.reason: The derivational discussion is meaningful, but the aligned local word is a proper divine name, so alternative derivations color rather than replace the local referent.

topics.headline: name before titles fixes the referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that power and praise are not free-floating ideas; they modify the named God believed in.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes both following titles adjectives modifying {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}), and the rows preserve the name-before-titles order.

topics.headline: belief in God exposes inversion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that a familiar belief-in-God relation becomes the sole grievance, echoing resentment-against-faith patterns such as 5:59 and 9:74.
topics.reason: The rows supply the 5:59 and 9:74 comparisons and the local phrase is exactly faith directed to God.

topics.headline: faith object becomes witness subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the immediate role shift: the God believed in at 85:8 appears as witnessing subject at 85:9.
topics.reason: The source rows give the concrete forward reference to 85:9, and the local word is the same divine name at the end of the faith clause.

words.gloss_range: the Mighty, unassailable, precious, and dignity-giving title as a genitive attribute of the God believed in
words.root_gloss_range: strength, invincibility, preciousness, difficulty of access, reinforcement, and granting honor; the local definite faʿīl title selects stable divine might while derivative branches add pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: faith-object phrase that carries the title chain

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَزِيزِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿazīzi}}) remains inside the {{ar:بِٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:bi-llāhi}}) complement as the first genitive attribute. It says that the God trusted by the believers is mighty, inaccessible to coercion, and precious beyond confiscation. The faʿīl shape makes that might stable rather than episodic; related strengthening and honor-giving branches sharpen the title, especially against 3:26 where might is granted by God. Placed between the faith-object and {{ar:ٱلْحَمِيدِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamīdi}}), the title relocates real power from the persecutors to God while pairing power with praise rather than tyranny. The compact title pair also echoes recognized formulas such as 34:6 and 14:1.

topics.headline: might modifies the faith-object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that might qualifies the God believed in, not a separate predicate outside the faith phrase.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses {{ar:ٱلْعَزِيزِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿazīzi}}) as a genitive divine attribute modifying {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}).

topics.headline: unassailable and precious might
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title joins invincibility with preciousness and reinforcement, while local form keeps the selected sense as stable divine might.
topics.reason: The root field supports preciousness and strengthening pressure, but the local surface is the definite faʿīl title, so derivative branches are narrowed to coloring force.

topics.headline: persecutor power is relativized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse answers coercion by locating unovercome power with the God believed in, with granted dignity in view (3:26).
topics.reason: The rows connect the title to faith, grievance, the divine name, and 3:26; locally it stands after persecuted faith and before praise.

topics.headline: might and praise arrive as a pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two final titles are heard and recognized together, joining power with praise in formulas such as 34:6 and 14:1.
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete formula references and the local titles are adjacent definite faʿīl attributes.

words.gloss_range: the Praiseworthy as the final genitive divine title, pairing moral worth with might and closing the ayah against blame

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَمِيدِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamīdi}}) is the final genitive attribute in the faith-object phrase, so the ayah lands on praiseworthiness. After {{ar:نَقَمُوا۟}} ({{tr:naqamū}}) has supplied hostile blame, this title gives the opposite evaluation: the One believed in is intrinsically worthy of praise, not dependent on persecutors' approval. Its faʿīl form makes praise stable, and its pairing with {{ar:ٱلْعَزِيزِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿazīzi}}) prevents the power-title from sounding like raw force. The same compact title pair has formulaic resonance, including 14:1, while the final long ī plus dāl cadence makes praise the heard closure and points forward by sound to {{ar:شَهِيدٌ}} ({{tr:shahīdun}}) in 85:9.

topics.headline: praise stays inside the faith phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that praiseworthiness modifies the God believed in as part of the same governed phrase.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:ٱلْحَمِيدِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamīdi}}) a second genitive divine attribute modifying {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}).

topics.headline: praise answers accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse does not merely deny blame; it ends with intrinsic praiseworthiness as the proper evaluation.
topics.reason: The local title is final and faʿīl, and the rows tie {{ar:ح م د}} ({{tr:ḥ-m-d}}) to praise, approval, and contrast with {{ar:ن ق م}} ({{tr:n-q-m}}).

topics.headline: power is morally praised
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing pair joins unassailable power with deserved praise, including formulaic resonance at 14:1.
topics.reason: The supplied rows identify the adjacent title pair and give 14:1 as a concrete formula reference.

topics.headline: praise becomes the heard landing

topics.reason: The word is final in 85:8, and the source row explicitly links its cadence forward to {{ar:شَهِيدٌ}} ({{tr:shahīdun}}) in 85:9.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Fault manufactured from trust.** `ن ق م` B001 supplies rejecting, resenting, and finding fault; `ء م ن` B002 supplies trusting assent. The exception construction leaves belief as the only alleged fault. I infer a normative inversion: the persecutors must recode trust as guilt to justify the mechanism of 85:4-7. The ayah reads as an exposure of grievance-production, not merely a statement that they disliked belief.

2. **A counterfeit requital reversed.** `ن ق م` B002 supplies punitive requital or vengeance. The perpetrators impose retaliatory punishment on believers, but 85:10 returns punishment to those who burned and did not turn. I infer the reversal of the directional arrow: human vengeance moves from persecutor to believer, while adjudicated requital moves back toward the persecutor. The fixed نقموا thus foreshadows the failure of their claim to punish.

3. **The object of faith is disclosed by the ordeal.** `ع ز ز` B001-B002 supply invulnerable honor and overcoming power; `ح م د` B002 supplies being found praiseworthy after testing, while B003 supplies one marked by many praiseworthy qualities. The next ayah expands divine dominion and witnessing, and 85:10 uses `ف ت ن` B001-B002, assay and fire. I infer that the ordeal intended to disprove belief instead tests and displays its object as unconquered and praiseworthy. العزيز الحميد therefore answers the persecutors' attempted verdict.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 85:10's `ف ت ن` B001-B002 pairing of assay and fire makes الحميد unexpectedly experimental: the ordeal intended as refutation becomes the condition under which praiseworthiness is disclosed. Ayah 85:16 then gives العزيز's overcoming power an effective mechanism, action joined to will. These later ayat correct a static title-reading; the two names answer the persecution causally by showing tested worth and unconstrained agency.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **An accusation that reverses under its own evidence.** Lexical evidence: `ن ق م` B001, “rejecting and faulting something”; `ء م ن` B002, “trusting assent and confirmation”; `ح م د` B001/B002, “praise” and “finding something praiseworthy or satisfactory.” Structural cue and role: the exceptive construction `ما ... إلا` isolates believing as the only alleged fault, while 85:7 supplies eyewitnesses and 85:10 supplies `ف ت ن` B001, assaying by trial. The trial exposes the charged quality, and `الحميد` supplies the opposite evaluation. Abductive move: I infer that what survives the assay is shown praiseworthy; the packet gives trial and praise but not an explicit verdict formula. Reading change: the sentence becomes a self-overturning indictment of the fault-finders rather than a neutral statement of motive.

2. **Power whose use is answerable to praise.** Lexical evidence: `ع ز ز` B001, “might and honor,” and B002, “overcoming and subduing,” are paired with `ح م د` B001, praise for praiseworthy action. Structural cue and role: the perpetrators’ operative force in 85:6–7 is followed by divine dominion and testimony in 85:9, then severe seizure in 85:12. `العزيز` supplies countervailing invulnerability; `الحميد` qualifies the manner and evaluation of its exercise. Abductive move: I infer that the pairing distinguishes praiseworthy power from coercive power; the adjectives do not narrate the intervention by themselves. Reading change: the titles function as a causal answer to persecution: effective power is present, but it is explicitly bound to praiseworthiness.

3. **Belief as sought security, not the cause of danger.** Lexical evidence: `ء م ن` B001, “settled security and trust.” Structural cue and role: the persecutors make believing the occasion of danger, yet 85:9 places all domains under divine dominion and 85:11 presents the believers’ eventual garden security. The root’s safety branch is therefore delayed rather than negated. Abductive move: I infer that trust relocates security from the immediate coercive scene to the larger sovereign frame. Reading change: `يؤمنوا` carries a paradoxical movement toward security through an act that triggers present exposure.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 85:10 supplied the decisive retrospective test: the assaying branch of `ف ت ن` makes the alleged fault undergo trial, while `الحميد` has already supplied its opposite evaluation. 85:12–13 then show that `العزيز` is not inert rank-language but power capable of seizure, initiation, and return.

baseline.text: Onlardan sırf güçlü ve övgüye layık Allah'a inandıkları için öç aldılar.

findings.text: İnancı tek suç sayan yapı, güveni suç diye yeniden adlandırarak zulme gerekçe üreten bir değer tersine çevirmesini açığa çıkarır.
Faillerin öç alma iddiası, sonraki karşılık ayetiyle yön değiştirir; cezalandırma yetkisi olduğunu sananlar karşılığın hedefi olur.
Ateşli sınama, Allah'ı güçsüz göstermek yerine O'nun yenilmez ve övgüye layık oluşunu olay içinde görünür kılar.
Güven arayışı, geçici tehlikeyi doğursa da daha geniş ilahi egemenlik içinde kalıcı güvenliğe yönelir.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimseye yaptığı kötülük veya suç yüzünden ceza vermek ya da acı çektirici bir karşılık uygulamaktır. Bu karşılık genel bir cezalandırma olabileceği gibi belirli bir haksızlık veya öldürme için öç alma biçimini de alabilir.

facets.statement: Yapılan kötülük veya suç yüzünden failine cezalandırıcı bir karşılık yöneltme.
Kişinin yaptığına karşılık sayılan bir cezayı ona uygulama.
Cezalandırıcı karşılığın belirli bir haksızlık için öç alma biçimine dönüşmesi.
Öldürme durumunda ölen kişi adına öç almayı anlatan daha dar kullanım.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, kötülük yapanı yaptığı yüzünden cezalandırmayı ve böylece ona cezayla karşılık vermeyi çekirdek sayar. Kapsam, genel cezalandırmadan belirli bir haksızlık veya öldürme için öç almaya uzanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadeleri bu dali yalniz korkunun kalkmasi olarak degil, kalbin yatismasi, guven verme, guvenilirlik, emanet edilen sey, guvenli yer ve dayanilir nitelik alanlariyla birlikte verir. Bu nedenle dalin cercevesi, guvenlik ve guvenilirlik ekseninde hem yalın hem de yapimli ve baglamli kullanislari ayirt ederek korunabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal inanma ya da dua cevabi degil; korkudan emin olma, guven verme ve guvenilir sayilma alanidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalin guven ve korkusuzluk anlamlari ile belirli yapimli ya da soz obegi kullanislari birlikte vardir; tanim bunlari tek bir dar kaliba indirgemez.

concept_map.definition: Korkunun kalkmasiyla kalbin yatismasi, birine guven verilmesi veya bir kimsenin ya da seyin guvenilir kabul edilmesidir. Bu alan guvenli yer, emanet edilen sey, kendisine guvenilen kisi ve dayanilir binek gibi bagimli uygulamalari da kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek korkuya karsi guven, ic yatiskinligi ve tehlikeden emin olma halidir.
Guven verme, birini kendi koruma ve teminat alani icine alma olarak kullanilir.
Guvenilirlik, ihanete karsi sadakat, emanet edilen sey ve kendisine guvenilen kisi anlamlarini dogurur.
Guvenin bulundugu yer, bir kimsenin emniyet icinde oldugu mesken veya siginak olarak adlandirilir.
Dayanikli ve aksamasindan korkulmayan deve kullanimi, guvenilirlik niteligini canli bir ornege uygular.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ortak olarak bu dali korkunun ziddi olan guven, kalbin yatismasi ve guven verme alaninda toplar. Ayni iddia guvenilir kisi, emanet, guvenli yer ve dayanilir binek gibi turemis ya da baglamli kullanislari da cekirdege baglar.

concept_map.definition: Bir haber, vaat veya hakikati dogru sayip ona icten kabul ile yonelmektir. Dini kullanista bu kabul, kalp, dil ve davranisla baglanan bir boyun egme ya da seriate girme anlami kazanabilir.

Dini alanlarda bu kabul, bildirilen yola girme ve ona baglanma adi olarak kullanilir.
Ilahi sifat kullaniminda vaat edilen odulu dogrulama veya guvenceyle bildirme boyutu one cikar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir kişiyi deneyim sonunda övülesi bulmayı, bir yeri yerleşme veya otlatma bakımından uygun bulmayı ve bir işi başkası için uygun görmeyi aynı olumlu değerlendirme ailesinde toplar. Dal çerçevesi bu katılımcı ve bağlam değişimlerini korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sözle övmeyi değil, kişi, yer veya iş hakkında olumlu bir sonuca varmayı anlatır; deneyim koşulu özellikle kişi kullanımında belirgindir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kişiyi deneyip övülesi bulma biçimi ile yer ve iş hakkında yalnız belirli tamlamalarda görülen uygunluk kullanımları ayrı yüzler olarak tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi deneyimden sonra övülesi bulma çekirdeğinden, bir yeri yerleşmeye veya otlatmaya elverişli bulma ve bir işi biri için uygun görme kullanımları doğar.

facets.statement: Bir kişi deneyim veya sınama sonrasında övülesi bulunur.
Bir yer, orada yaşamak veya hayvan otlatmak bakımından elverişli bulunur.
Bir işin başkası için uygun görülüp görülmediği sorulur veya uygun görüldüğü bildirilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak anlatımı olumlu bulma sonucunu üç kapsamda gösterir: deneyimden sonra övülesi bulunan kişi, yaşamaya ya da otlatmaya elverişli bulunan yer ve başkası için uygun görülmesi sorulan veya bildirilen iş.

concept_gloss.text: deneyip övülesi ya da uygun bulma
concept_gloss.applicability: Kişi hakkındaki deneyim sonucunu çekirdeğe alır; yerin elverişliliğini ve bir işin başkası için uygun görülmesini de bağlama bağlı kapsamlar olarak taşır.

error_profile.preserves: Olumlu bulma sonucunu, deneyim koşulunu ve kişi, yer ile iş kapsamlarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir yerin kullanım için elverişli sayıldığı veya bir işin bir kişi için onaylandığı bağlamlarda doğaldır.

error_profile.adds: Kaynakta bulunmayan genel amaç ve nesneler için sınırsız uygunluk kullanımını çağrıştırabilir.
